assertions.text: Discount ladder, and traveller eligibility are in separate tables. Rolling window counting as a third table is desirable.
assertions.evidence: discountForTripCount, countSingleTicketsInWindow, and discountForCategoryAndTripCount are three distinct @TableTest methods.

assertions.text: Children's flat 20% discount is represented — either as a row in the eligibility table or a separate note. It does not follow the ladder.
assertions.evidence: "Child gets a flat discount regardless of trips | CHILD | {1, 5, 40} | 20"

assertions.text: The discount ladder has multiple tiers derived from the 'every fifth trip' rule, with boundary values or value sets showing which ticket counts produce which discount. The maximum 40% discount is represented.
assertions.evidence: "Exactly at the cap | 40 | 40" and "Beyond the cap stays capped | {41, 45, 100} | 40"

assertions.text: The 30-day rolling window boundary is tested: a ticket at exactly 30 days is included, at 31 days is excluded.
assertions.evidence: "Exactly 30 days ago is still in window | [30/SINGLE/ZONE_1] | 1" and "31 days ago has fallen out of the window | [31/SINGLE/ZONE_1] | 0"

assertions.text: The 30-day window is exercised at time-of-purchase granularity, not whole days only.
assertions.evidence: TypeConverter uses `PURCHASE_TIME.minusDays(daysAgo)` and all rows use whole-day values like 29, 30, 31 — no sub-day distinction is tested.

assertions.text: Value sets in the tier table contain exactly the values that produce the same discount. No cross-tier contamination.
assertions.evidence: "Within first tier | {6, 7, 8, 9} | 5" and "Within second tier | {11, 12, 13, 14} | 10" — sets align correctly per tier.

assertions.text: The discount ladder table uses value sets for the ticket count column to group counts within the same tier.
assertions.evidence: "Below first tier | {1, 2, 3, 4} | 0" and "Within seventh tier | {36, 37, 38, 39} | 35"

assertions.text: The tier-to-discount mapping is expressed once — not repeated across multiple tables.
assertions.evidence: discountForCategoryAndTripCount re-enumerates tier mapping: "Adult at a tier | ADULT | 10 | 10" and "Adult and senior are capped the same | {ADULT, SENIOR} | 45 | 40", duplicating the ladder table's mapping.

assertions.text: @DisplayName is present on test methods, OR method names read as clear descriptive titles when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: 4 @TableTest method name(s) read as descriptive titles (no @DisplayName needed)

assertions.text: @Description is present on at least the class or the tier method and provides context beyond what the table rows already express.
assertions.evidence: "The trip ladder: every 5th single ticket in the rolling 30-day window (counting the ticket being purchased now) raises the discount by 5%, up to a 40% cap."

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
assertions.evidence: Annotations in correct order: @DisplayName, @Description, @TableTest

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: @Description uses text block or is short single-line

assertions.text: The eligibility/passenger-type table includes a Zone column (or equivalent) with a value set to show that the discount applies regardless of zone.
assertions.evidence: discountForCategoryAndTripCount table columns are only "Traveler Category | Trips In Window | Discount?" — no Zone column present.

assertions.text: The rolling-window counting concern shows by row that a past purchase's zone does not affect whether it counts toward the travel count
assertions.evidence: Zone does not affect the count | [1/SINGLE/ZONE_1, 2/SINGLE/ZONE_2, 3/SINGLE/ZONE_3] | 3

assertions.text: Adult and senior are expressed as a value set {ADULT, SENIOR}
assertions.evidence: Adult and senior are capped the same | {ADULT, SENIOR} | 45 | 40

assertions.text: All 9 discount tiers are represented in the ladder table
assertions.evidence: Rows only cover 0,5,10,35,40; tiers 15,20,25,30 (e.g. 'Exactly at third/fourth/fifth/sixth tier') are absent from discountForTripCount table

assertions.text: Each tier is expressed as a single row with a value set for ticket counts
assertions.evidence: Exactly at first tier | 5 | 5' and 'Within first tier | {6, 7, 8, 9} | 5' are two separate rows for the same tier

assertions.text: The rolling window table expresses time relatively
assertions.evidence: Exactly 30 days ago is still in window | [30/SINGLE/ZONE_1] | 1

assertions.text: Multiple tables each addressing a distinct concern
assertions.evidence: discountForTripCount, countSingleTicketsInWindow, discountForCategoryAndTripCount, calculatesDiscountEndToEnd are separate @TableTest methods

assertions.text: Each table has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules
assertions.evidence: countSingleTicketsInWindow rows only vary History and ticket type, not mixing category or ladder concerns

assertions.text: The build file (build.gradle) includes org.tabletest:tabletest-junit as a test dependency
assertions.evidence: Build file contains tabletest-junit

assertions.text: Cell values make the rule falsifiable
assertions.evidence: Discount? values vary across rows, e.g. '0,5,10,35,40' in discountForTripCount, not a fixed constant

assertions.text: A reader can state the rule from the table alone
assertions.evidence: Description states '30 days', 'SINGLE-ticket', and 'every 5th single ticket ... raises the discount by 5%, up to a 40% cap'

assertions.text: Each @DisplayName (or fallback method name) states what the code under test does
assertions.evidence: void discountForTripCount(...) and void countSingleTicketsInWindow(...) name the computation performed, not a domain fact

assertions.text: The generated test code compiles successfully against the project scaffolding
assertions.evidence: Compilation succeeded

assertions.text: A value the rule's outcome depends on, and which the table holds constant for every row, must be visible as a column or named in the @DisplayName/@Description as deliberately held fixed.
assertions.evidence: "Description(... All rows share the same purchaseTime...)" explicitly declares the fixed PURCHASE_TIME constant for the end-to-end table; other tables use relative 'days ago' so the absolute PURCHASE_TIME value cannot affect outcomes, and the hardcoded ADULT category in the PastPurchase converter is irrelevant to the ticket-type/window counting logic under test.

assertions.text: When a title or description quantifies over a domain, the rows must actually cover that domain.
assertions.evidence: "CHILD always gets a flat 20% discount, independent of travel frequency" is discharged by the row 'Child gets a flat discount regardless of trips | CHILD | {1, 5, 40} | 20'; 'Zone must never affect the count' is discharged by rows using ZONE_1/ZONE_2/ZONE_3 including 'Zone does not affect the count | [1/SINGLE/ZONE_1, 2/SINGLE/ZONE_2, 3/SINGLE/ZONE_3] | 3'.
